newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Bond reaffirms Thomson ratings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Bond reaffirms Thomson ratings.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Friday it reaffirmed the ratings on Thomson Corp commercial paper at A-1, unsecured debentures at A(High) and cumulative preference shares P-1(Low).
CBRS said the affirmations follow an extensive review of the company's operations and recent acquisitions.
The acquisition of legal publisher West Publishing Co has shifted Thomson into a provider of specialized information to professional audiences.

"The shift has significantly reduced the company's dependence on cyclical, advertising-related markets (advertising as a percentage of total sales has dropped to approximately 10 percent)," the agency said.

It said the US$3.4 billion acquisition of West was financed by bank facilities which have been partly repaid by proceeds from US$1.5 billion in divestitures in 1995 and 1996, which may be augmented by another US$200 million due to be generated from sales already announced this year.
The debt-to-equity ratio was about 0.53:0.47 percent at the end of 1996 versus 0.46:0.54 percent in 1995.

"To reduce its indebtedness as a faster pace than what its substantial operating cash flow alone might permit, Thomson completed a C$450 million issue of perpetual preferred shares on November 21, 1996, and could sell some additional assets, if required, to face debt maturities," CBRS said.

The US$150 million in consolidated 1997 maturities are manageable. Debenture and note maturities are well-scattered over the 1998-2006 period. Longer-term public debt will continue to replace bank debt progressively as permitted by capital market conditions.
